observable_outcome: An emergency stop stops planning and preparation. Measured at 76cfa91, it does not: Service.Plan (internal/application/service.go:882-966) and Service.Prepare (service.go:986-1041) contain no reference to domain.Permit, domain.Controls, domain.EffectiveControl or domain.EffectFromPermit, yet Plan writes the parent Requirement and creates an Increment and Prepare moves that Increment to the only status a Claim accepts -- so under emergency-stop, the mode docs/product/definition.md section 7 describes as stopping every repository, every worker and every version, a caller still moves canonical state. V2-082 measured this and left it logged rather than asserted (internal/application/framing_test.go:565, naming V2-085 as the owner of the repair). The repair is exactly two domain.Permit evaluations of kind claim, one in each command, against a ControlTarget and revision resolved inside the same transaction from the Requirement's own Repository link and domain.EffectiveControl -- never from the request, so no request field, no route and no transport contract change. Nothing is passed to domain.EffectFromPermit and no outbox item is staged, because neither command asks anything outside the control plane to act and the allow-only closure would wrongly deny both under pause-intake. What fixes the outcome is an asserted seven-mode table for each command in a new test file -- allow ALLOWS, pause-intake ALLOWS, pause-claim DENIES, graceful-stop DENIES, immediate-stop DENIES, emergency-stop DENIES, cancel DENIES -- cross-checked in the same run against the package's permitAllowedTable mirror and against Capture's measured intake behaviour, which must DISAGREE under pause-intake; every denied cell asserted to be domain.ErrControlDenied AND to leave the store byte-unchanged; and framing_test.go's logged probe converted into an assertion under its existing name. The eight-kind stop matrix and docs/product/definition.md are untouched.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Re-measure the baseline yourself before writing any code, and record every disagreement rather than the number written here. (i) `awk 'NR>=882 && NR<=1042' internal/application/service.go | grep -n 'Permit\|Controls\|EffectiveControl\|EffectFromPermit'` returns NO match, i.e. Plan and Prepare are permit-free; report the exact line span you measured for each function. (ii) The non-test census of `domain.Permit(` and `domain.EffectFromPermit(` is eleven call sites: internal/application/framing.go:183, repository.go:128, outbox.go:448, human_input.go:644, service.go:415, :664, :824, :1228, :1469, :1669 and the EffectFromPermit at service.go:1673; report the count and the list, and report that Plan and Prepare appear in neither. (iii) internal/domain/control.go permitAllowed is at :266-281 and EffectFromPermit's allow-only test is at :301; PermitKind.SideEffect() is at :199-201 and returns false for PermitClaim. (iv) quota.MutationUsage is Reads 32 / Writes 16 at internal/quota/quota.go:62. A2. Reproduce the defect yourself before repairing it, and record the argv and the verbatim verdict. With an effective control mode of emergency-stop engaged on a ScopeInstallation Control Intent, call Service.Plan and then Service.Prepare and record: the error returned by each (expected nil), whether the Requirement's canonical state moved, and whether the Increment reached IncrementReady. Record this as the BEFORE row of a before/after table. Do not write the repair until this row is measured.

A3. The Permit in Plan. Inside Service.Plan's s.mutate callback, in this exact order: (1) the existing u.Idempotency replay and fingerprint-conflict refusal FIRST, unchanged; (2) the existing Requirement load and ExpectedRequirementVersion check, unchanged; (3) MOVE the existing u.RequirementRepositoryLink read (currently at service.go:947-960, after the aggregate is staged) to here, build domain.ControlTarget{InstallationID: s.config.InstallationID, RepositoryID: linked}, read u.Controls(ctx), compute domain.EffectiveControl(controls, target), take the revision from it (0 when not Found) and evaluate domain.Permit(effective, domain.PermitRequest{Kind: domain.PermitClaim, Target: target, ControlRevision: revision, Resource: req.RequirementID}); (4) only then stage the Requirement, the Increment, the canonical target and the event, exactly as today. Add NO field to PlanRequest. Pass nothing to domain.EffectFromPermit and stage no OutboxItem. On denial return the error and stage nothing.

A4. The Permit in Prepare. Inside Service.Prepare's s.mutate callback, same order: idempotency replay first, then the Increment load and ExpectedVersion check, then resolve the link from the Increment's own parent -- u.RequirementRepositoryLink(ctx, inc.RequirementID.String()) -- build the target, read u.Controls, compute domain.EffectiveControl, and evaluate domain.Permit with Kind domain.PermitClaim and Resource req.IncrementID; then domain.DecideIncrement and the save and the event, unchanged. Add NO field to PrepareRequest. An Increment whose parent Requirement has no Repository link yields an empty RepositoryID, which is NOT an error.

A5. The seven-mode table, asserted per command, in a NEW file internal/application/planning_permit_test.go. One fresh Service and store per mode. Establish the Requirement and the Increment while the mode is still allow (Capture is intake-gated and would itself be denied under most of these modes, which would measure the wrong thing), then engage the Control Intent, then attempt Plan on a second fresh Requirement and Prepare on a second proposed Increment. Assert for EACH of the seven modes and for EACH of the two commands: allow ALLOWED, pause-intake ALLOWED, pause-claim DENIED, graceful-stop DENIED, immediate-stop DENIED, emergency-stop DENIED, cancel DENIED. Write the want table out explicitly as a named map rather than deriving it, and cross-check it in the same run against the package's existing permitAllowedTable mirror (internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go:242) for domain.PermitClaim; both must agree. Assert that exactly 2 of the 7 modes allow each command.

A6. Every DENIED cell asserted three ways, because two of them are what non_goals item 2 forbids. For each denied cell: (a) errors.Is(err, domain.ErrControlDenied) is true -- not ErrStaleVersion, not ErrNotFound, not a validation error; (b) the Requirement (for Plan) and the Increment (for Prepare) are byte-unchanged by reflect.DeepEqual against the value read immediately before the attempt, including Version and, for Plan, the Increments slice; (c) the store's event count and outbox row count are unchanged, and no idempotency record was written -- prove (c) by replaying the SAME request_id under allow afterwards and asserting it executes for real rather than replaying a stored response.

A7. The boundary that is the whole argument for the kind, asserted where it happens. Under pause-intake, at the same control revision and in the same test run: Plan is ALLOWED, Prepare is ALLOWED, and a fresh Service.Capture is DENIED. Log the two errors verbatim. Under emergency-stop, all three are DENIED. If pause-intake denies Plan or Prepare, or allows Capture, stop and escalate: the kind is wrong and the design must be revisited, not the assertion.

A13. The closed-set discipline, if any want set is touched. Widening a closed-set guard is a MEASUREMENT, not a weakening -- but only under three conditions, and all three must be recorded: the set stays CLOSED (an unlisted member still fails), the only change is added entries plus a comment giving the reason for each, and nothing else in the guard changes. This task is not expected to need any such widening; if one appears necessary, record which set, which entries and why, and confirm the three conditions by assertion.

A14. Determinism and quota. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new or modified test; every clock is injected and every wait is a bounded deadline poll reusing an idiom already in the package. A measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold. Separately: the in-memory adapter never calls quota.Counter.TrueUp, so quota.ReadTransactionUsage (Reads 6001, Writes 1) admits only FOUR read transactions per budget day. If any new test reads through Service more than four times, advance the injected clock; do NOT weaken the assertion or drop the read. That adapter defect is V2-087's and is not fixed here.

constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

Do not edit internal/domain. Add no PermitKind, no ControlMode, no RequirementStatus, no IncrementStatus and no lease transition, and change no allowed() list. Everything this task needs already exists: domain.Permit, domain.PermitClaim, domain.EffectiveControl and domain.ErrControlDenied. If the repair appears to need a domain edit, the design was departed from: stop and escalate.

The permit kind is domain.PermitClaim for BOTH commands, evaluated with domain.Permit ALONE. Do not choose domain.PermitIntake: pause-intake means take no new work in and finish what you already have (docs/product/definition.md:142), and planning an already-captured Requirement's Increment is finishing what you have. Do not pass anything to domain.EffectFromPermit: it requires the effective mode to be exactly allow (internal/domain/control.go:301), which would wrongly deny both commands under pause-intake. Do not stage an OutboxItem: PermitKind.SideEffect() is false for claim and nothing outside the control plane is asked to act.

Do not accept a control revision, a repository id or a timestamp from the caller. Add NO field to PlanRequest or PrepareRequest. The revision comes from domain.EffectiveControl inside the transaction, the repository comes from the Requirement's own link, and a caller-supplied value for either is refused rather than honoured -- domain.Permit requires the revision to be EXACTLY the authoritative one, so a caller-supplied field would deny for a reason unrelated to the owner's intent.

Do not turn a refusal into a silent no-op, and do not turn a completed operation into a refusal. A denied call returns an error errors.Is can match against domain.ErrControlDenied AND leaves the store byte-unchanged AND writes no idempotency record. The u.Idempotency replay stays FIRST, ahead of the Permit, so a retry of a request that already committed still replays its committed response after a stop is engaged.

Do not change what either command does when permission is granted. PlanResponse and PrepareResponse keep their exact shapes and their exact success values; the same documents are written, the same event types recorded and the same versions produced.

Do not add a kind to stopMatrixKinds and do not change wantStopMatrixCells (56), wantStopModeAllowedCounts or wantStopModeAllowedTotal (12). internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go must be byte-unchanged. docs/product/definition.md:155-162 states those figures and names TestStopModeByKindMatrix as their verifier, so widening the matrix would silently falsify a product document and enrol this task in the docs chain. The new table lives in internal/application/planning_permit_test.go, exactly as V2-082 put start-framing's table in framing_test.go.

Do not add a route, a read model field, an owner-console control or a document. internal/api/**, contracts/**, internal/web/** and docs/** are prohibited BY DESIGN: Plan and Prepare have no HTTP route, openapi-v1.yaml:6-8 declares increment decomposition deliberately absent from the public surface, and a denied Plan leaves exactly the state an uncalled Plan leaves, so no response shape changes.

That it reaches them through a caller the component fabricates for itself (internal/runner/orchestrator.go:39, Subject 'runner-local-owner') is a separate defect owned by V2-086: record it, do not fix it, and do not relabel the caller.

Do not relax the guard to make a test pass. Classify every failure as the intended guard firing or as a fixture that never set a control mode, report the classification, and fix only the fixture -- by establishing the Increment before the Control Intent. Widening the accepted modes, accepting a caller revision, deleting a cell from the table or weakening an assertion is a design change and requires an escalation, not an edit.

Clocks are injected, waiting is expressed only as bounded deadline polling reusing an existing idiom in the package, and a measured duration is logged as an observation and never asserted as a threshold.

A test that needs more must advance the injected clock; it must not weaken an assertion, skip a read or raise a budget. internal/quota is prohibited and that adapter defect is V2-087's.
